title: Woman Admits Trying to Scam Wes Edens for $1.2 Billion
summary: A woman pleaded guilty to fraud in connection with a plot to extort Fortress Investment Group co-founder Wes Edens out of more than $1.2 billion by threatening to release videos of them having sex.

title: Huel CEO on Danone Deal and Expansion to US Retail
summary: Huel CEO James McMaster discusses Danone’s roughly $1.2 billion acquisition of the UK-based meal-replacement and protein-shake maker. He says Huel established local manufacturing and warehouses when it entered the U.S. about eight years ago, and has since grown internationally; the company views Danone as the right partner to take it to its next stage. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Loop Capital CEO on Expanding Athlete Wealth Platform
summary: Loop Capital is buying $450 million in client assets from Lifeline Capital to expand its wealth management business and serve more athletes and entertainers. Founder, Chairman and CEO Jim Reynolds said the firm encourages athletes to invest in companies and gain ownership rather than rely on short-term endorsement payments. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

summary: A Canadian consumer lender has left creditors with potential claims of more than C$613 million ($430 million), while a court-appointed receiver struggles to account for the firms’ loans and determine how investor money was used.

title: Why Inflation Numbers Are Disappointing
summary: While inflation numbers might not be disastrous, they’re still disappointing and moving in the wrong direction. Bloomberg Opinion columnist John Authers explains where this leaves the US, and if it will lead to any more rate hikes from the Fed. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Container Ship Sinks in Strait of Hormuz as Attacks Ramp Up
summary: A cargo ship sank in the Strait of Hormuz after a strike that sparked a fire and the evacuation of crew members, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore said.

title: Bitcoin Slides as Wall Street Risk Pullback Tests Bullish Turn
summary: Bitcoin fell as much as 2.3% toward the lower end of its recent trading range, caught in a broader retreat from risk assets even as crypto analysts have turned sharply more bullish on the token.

title: Oil Gains as Middle East, Russia Hostilities Imperil Flows
summary:
Oil gained Wednesday as hostilities intensified from Russia to the Middle East, threatening supply flows that only recently recovered to near pre-war levels.

Brent traded above $106 after Iran-backed Houthi rebels launched missile and drone strikes across Saudi Arabia, including a hit that damaged Saudi Aramco’s headquarters. That added to an escalation in Iranian attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz that’s threatening a rebound in Gulf supply. We discuss the latest energy headlines with Rob Barnett, Senior Energy Analyst for Bloomberg Intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stocks Fall on Inflation Woes as Chip Rout Deepens: Markets Wrap
summary: Stocks fell the most since July as a selloff in chipmakers extended a decline that was fueled by wagers the Federal Reserve will keep lifting interest rates to fight inflation.

title: Gold Slumps as Faster US Inflation Stokes Fed Rate Hike Wagers
summary: Gold slumped after US consumer prices jumped the most in five months, reigniting worries that the Federal Reserve will need to raise interest rates further to combat inflation.

title: Dollar Advances to Highest Since May 2025 on Fed Hike Views
summary: The dollar strengthened to the highest level in over a year as a hot US inflation reading pushed traders to add to bets that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates.

summary: The Russell 2000 Index entered a correction with Wednesday’s plunge as rising inflation and interest rates push the riskiest stocks in the market below important averages.

title: SEC Approves Cboe’s KPI Prediction-Market Bets Via Robinhood

title: Treasuries Recover Most of Their Post-CPI Losses as Stocks Fall

title: Copper Edges Lower After World’s Biggest Mine Averts Strike
summary: Copper slipped after BHP Group’s Escondida mine in Chile, the world’s largest, averted a strike that would have tightened supply as the industry struggles to keep pace with demand from data centers and power grids.
